newsitem.title: UK: BAA May passengers up 8.9 pct to 8.9 mln.
newsitem.headline: BAA May passengers up 8.9 pct to 8.9 mln.

text.p: British airports operator BAA Plc said on Thursday its seven UK airports handled a total of 8.9 million passengers in May, an increase of 8.9 percent on May 1996.
The total cargo tonnage handled rose by 6.5 percent to 131,031 tonnes in May, BAA said.

It said London airport Gatwick recorded an overall increase of 17.2 percent in passenger traffic, and for the first time has handled a total of 25 million passengers in a 12 month period, with strong growth in all market sectors.

"May's traffic figures highlight four success stories - the effectiveness of BAA's three London airports working together as a system; the emergence of Gatwick as a major European hub in its own right; (London airport) Stansted's breakthrough above the five million annual passenger level and a general recovery of the European charter market," said BAA Chief Executive John Egan.

Stansted, a small airport which handles mostly short-hop European traffic, experienced an overall increase of 12.1 percent, and for the first time handled five million passengers in a 12 month period, BAA said.
May passenger traffic at London's busiest airport Heathrow was up by 4.7 percent as 4.8 million travellers past through the gates.

BAA said the European Charter market increased by 16.6 percent, indicating a sharp recovery in the Mediterranean package holiday market. Traffic on North Atlantic services increased by 12.8 percent and other Long Haul routes increased by 11.7 percent.
Air travel to and from Eire grew rapidly with an 18.8 percent increase while European scheduled and domestic traffic increased by 4.6 percent and 4.4 percent respectively.
